general_rules.description: Internal team members (same domain @strategyco.com) receive casual greetings (first name only) and casual closings (initials or 'Cheers'), regardless of seniority.

External clients and senior stakeholders receive formal greetings ('Dear [First Name]' or 'Dear [Title] [Last Name]') with full signature block closings ('Best regards, James Conseil Senior Consultant StrategyCo | London').
Administrative/support staff (Emma Phillips) receive casual tone with brief, action-oriented requests and minimal formality despite being internal.
Emails to clients include detailed context, structured sections with bullet points, and clear action items or next steps.
Internal team communications are concise, use numbered action items, and often include direct feedback or coaching language ('Well done', 'Good work', 'Nice job').
Travel and logistics requests to Emma are ultra-brief with specific details (dates, times, preferences) and no greeting formality.
Client-facing emails include full signature block with title and company; internal emails omit signature block entirely.
Emails to non-English speaking contacts (Klaus Weber, Takeshi Yamamoto) maintain formal English tone with careful, respectful language and cultural acknowledgment.
Project status updates to internal stakeholders (Richard Hayes) use bullet-point summaries with financial metrics, risk flags, and utilisation data.
Feedback on deliverables to team members is specific, references slide numbers, and includes both praise and constructive suggestions.
